stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: 9 headlines, which is about its normal of 31.5 after 30 days running. Continuing coverage rather than escalation - gold has priced this.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.
stories.spoken: Iran, and the US and Israel
stories.spoken_why: It reaches gold through three channels at once: the haven bid, lower real yields, and the risk to oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz.

asia.read: Asian equities are mixed, averaging +0.57% - no clear overnight lead for London. Gold moved +0.35% overnight in a 0.72% range, and comes into London near the top of it. asia.caveat: Measured from 00:00 UK to 13:40. Tokyo closes around 07:00 UK and Hong Kong around 09:00, so this is a session finishing rather than one that has finished.

correlations.regime: Gold and the dollar are running at -0.38. That is the textbook inverse relationship, so dollar moves are doing real work on the price. Against the S&P it is +0.50. Gold is trading WITH risk assets rather than against them, so it is behaving as a liquidity asset right now, not a hedge - do not rely on it to offset an equity drawdown while that holds.

profile.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
profile.what: Survey of purchasing managers. Above 50 means expansion. Released 15:00 UK.
profile.who: Institute for Supply Management, first business day of the month
profile.why_gold: A timely growth signal that arrives before the hard data. Weakness feeds recession pricing, which is usually gold-supportive.
profile.watch: The prices-paid and new-orders sub-indices carry more information than the headline.
profile.gotchas: Manufacturing is a small share of US output, so the survey overstates its own importance.
